The test image shows a corn stalk broken/split open at a node with:
- Shredded, fibrous pith tissue (tan/straw colored)
- Numerous tiny black dots on the stalk surface/rind
- No gray/charcoal coloration

Top candidates: **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (small black pycnidia + shredded pith) or **Charcoal_stalk_rot** (gray appearance with sclerotia). Let me compare reference images.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows a corn stalk broken/collapsed at a node with:
- **Shredded, fibrous tan/straw-colored pith** — rules out Charcoal stalk rot (which is gray)
- **Numerous tiny black dots on the internode rind** — these are pycnidia, characteristic of Diplodia
- **Stalk lodging/collapse** — consistent with late-season stalk rot
- No shiny black rind discoloration (rules out Anthracnose)
- No whole-node blackening (rules out Physoderma)
- No gray charcoal-like tissue (rules out Charcoal stalk rot)

The Diplodia reference confirms: broken stalks, small black pycnidia on internode surface, shredded tan pith — an excellent match.
